display.purpose: Didot for banner titles and a working page's headline and numerals, at 1rem or larger only.

title.purpose: Baskerville Semibold for subtitles, diagram labels, and card titles.

body.purpose: Baskerville for a working page's body text.

label.purpose: Compact system sans for section labels and chips, never smaller than 0.7rem.

control.purpose: Compact system sans for buttons, filters, fields, and metadata.

mono.purpose: System monospace for code diffs and key caps.

motion.name: chevron-turn
motion.purpose: Turns a disclosure chevron when its card or drawer opens; off under reduced motion.

components.name: Card
components.description: A white sheet that carries one item to decide: rank, title, metadata, and the controls that record the decision.
components.html:
1Add the frontier chart

One item to decide, on a white sheet held by a hairline.

components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; color: #042458; border: 1px solid rgb(71 87 122 / 0.32); border-radius: 2px; padding: 22px 24px 24px; font: 1rem/1.5 Baskerville, 'Libre Baskerville', 'Baskerville Old Face', Georgia, serif; } .ds-card h2 { margin: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; font: 600 1.2rem/1.3 Baskerville, 'Libre Baskerville', 'Baskerville Old Face', Georgia, serif; } .ds-rank { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; flex: none; width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid #47577A; color: #47577A; font: 400 1rem/1 Didot, 'Bodoni 72', 'Bodoni MT', Georgia, serif; } .ds-card p { margin: 10px 0 0; } .ds-collapse { margin-top: 10px; } .ds-collapse summary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 36px; padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; list-style: none; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #7C87A0; border-radius: 2px; font: 600 0.82rem/1.5 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-collapse summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-collapse summary::before { content: ""; flex: none; width: 7px; height: 7px; margin: 0 3px; border-right: 1.5px solid #47577A; border-bottom: 1.5px solid #47577A; transform: rotate(-45deg); transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-collapse[open] summary::before { transform: rotate(45deg); } .ds-collapse summary:hover { border-color: #47577A; } .ds-collapse summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0050CC; outline-offset: 2px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-collapse summary::before { transition: none; } }

components.name: Control Button
components.description: A button or filter on a working page, edged in Control Border so its edge reaches 3:1 against the paper.
components.css: .ds-control { min-height: 36px; padding: 6px 12px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #042458; border: 1px solid #7C87A0; border-radius: 2px; font: 0.82rem/1.5 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-control:hover { border-color: #47577A; } .ds-control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0050CC; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Records one choice; the chosen option is a Raven Navy fill with Chalk text.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #7C87A0; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-seg button { min-height: 36px; padding: 6px 13px; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid #7C87A0; background: none; color: #042458; font: 0.82rem/1.5 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-seg button:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-seg button:hover { background: #E3E9F7; } .ds-seg button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #042458; color: #F6F7FA; font-weight: 650; } .ds-seg button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0050CC; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A one-line note field with the same height and edge as the other controls.
components.html: <input class="ds-field" type="text" aria-label="Note" placeholder="Add a note">
components.css: .ds-field { width: 240px; max-width: 100%; min-height: 36px; padding: 6px 10px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #042458; caret-color: #0050CC; border: 1px solid #7C87A0; border-radius: 2px; font: 0.82rem/1.5 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #47577A; } .ds-field:hover { border-color: #47577A; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0050CC; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip and Seal
components.description: A metadata chip, and the small Signal Orange seal that marks what needs the operator, with its meaning in Signal Ink.

components.name: Factor Pills

components.name: Diff Lines
components.description: Added and removed code lines in the green and red readers expect; each pair reaches 7:1.

narrative.overview:
The Rookery looks like a natural-history field manual laid over a working draft table. Cool mist-blue paper, engraved navy corvids, graphite mechanisms, and measured construction lines make the work feel studied and practical rather than mythical or corporate. The result should make the technical system clear while retaining the warmth and memory of a hand-kept field guide.

Every illustration explains an operation. Huginn and Muninn carry, inspect, install, select, or return knowledge; they do not pose beside an abstract idea. Routes and mechanisms show the order of work, where observation happens, and how feedback returns. One restrained orange signal marks the intervention, dispatch, or return that matters most. Scenes may change across repository-owned explanatory visuals. Each should show the same connected system, with evidence moving forward and distinct feedback paths improving future work.
keyCharacteristics: Cool drafting paper with faint grain, registration marks, and construction geometry.
Natural-history corvid engraving paired with graphite field mechanisms.
Cobalt paths that distinguish delivery from feedback and a scarce orange signal that explains intervention or return.
Wide, calm compositions with enough negative space to survive GitHub rendering at reduced sizes.
Characters whose physical action carries the meaning of the explanation.

rules.name: The Orange Means Intervention Rule
rules.body: Orange identifies the action, handoff, or return that changes the state of the workflow; it is never a general-purpose accent.

rules.name: The Ink Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Raven Navy explains the subject, Route Cobalt explains movement, and Drafting Graphite explains supporting structure.

rules.name: The Two Papers Rule
rules.body: Mist Paper carries a scene; Chalk Paper carries data. A figure whose job is to be read, not looked at, goes on Chalk. Text inks must reach 4.5:1 on their paper, and Drafting Graphite does on both.

rules.name: The Printed-In Rule
rules.body: Lettering must share the illustration's ink hierarchy and perspective while remaining real typography; never ask the raster artwork layer to render essential copy.

rules.name: The Family Restraint Rule
rules.body: Use one display treatment and one explanatory treatment within an asset. Name an exact font family only when the editable source uses it.

rules.name: The Layered Type Rule
rules.body: Keep essential lettering as real typography over a text-free illustration plate, retain the editable source, and export the shipped raster losslessly.

rules.name: The Causal System Rule
rules.body: Show the five delivery jobs as an ordered sequence and each feedback process as its own path to the stages or input it changes. Never force distinct feedback loops into a false serial sequence, and never flatten the system into repeated equal containers.

rules.name: The Reduced-Size Test
rules.body: At ordinary GitHub content width, the five-job delivery order, repository-wide improvement path, and return of a better question to Research must remain understandable before a reader zooms into the engraving detail.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: Create depth with physical overlap, perspective, and line density; do not simulate it with product-UI drop shadows or glow.

rules.name: The Mechanism Has Consequence Rule
rules.body: Every aperture, gate, jig, ring, or bridge must make the stage's operation clearer; remove decorative machinery that does not change the explanation.

dos: Do give Huginn or Muninn an action essential to the explanation, such as carrying a dispatch, operating a mechanism, inspecting a handoff, or returning a signal.
Do use Route Cobalt and shape or direction together, so paths remain understandable without color.
Do distinguish the Delivery Sequence, Repository Learning Loop, and Personal Learning Loop by position, labels, direction, and mechanism as well as color.
Do keep Signal Orange scarce and attach it to one meaningful intervention or return.
Do preserve calm negative space and a strong silhouette before adding paper grain, coordinates, hatching, or registration marks.
Do write meaningful alt text that states the mechanism, sequence, and return represented by the image.
donts: Don't turn the workflow into a generic equal-card flowchart or consulting-deck diagram.
Don't present Research, Plan, Design, Build, Ship, Maintain, and Learn as one seven-step serial loop; Maintain and Learn are distinct feedback loops with different destinations.
Don't pose a raven beside an idea it is not performing; removing the bird should break the explanation.
Don't use broad orange fills, multiple competing accents, glossy gradients, or interface-style shadows.
Don't drift into novelty mascot art or Norse-fantasy ornament that overwhelms the technical mechanism.
Don't imply that the system learns autonomously; the return mythology supports the operator's deliberate learning loop.
